steps.title: Privilege gateway
steps.what: A Remote Agent application fronts an A2A agent, which publishes a public agent card and a JSON-RPC endpoint.
steps.why: Agents that call other agents need the same sign-in, policy and logging as tool traffic, so agent-to-agent calls are not an ungoverned side channel.

steps.title: Gateway log
steps.what: The gateway runs three checks in order: sign-in or a valid key, a policy covering the caller and the app, then the app's Auth Mode check.
steps.why: Agents that call other agents need the same sign-in, policy and logging as tool traffic, so agent-to-agent calls are not an ungoverned side channel.

steps.title: AgentCard discovery
steps.what: AgentCard discovery is one of the components this feature uses.
steps.why: Agents that call other agents need the same sign-in, policy and logging as tool traffic, so agent-to-agent calls are not an ungoverned side channel.

steps.title: Distinct A2A key scope
steps.what: The Ping deck adds that A2A endpoints run through the same gateway as MCP, with agent access keys carrying a distinct scope, so a key permitted to reach a peer agent does not thereby reach every MCP server in the tenant.
steps.why: Agents that call other agents need the same sign-in, policy and logging as tool traffic, so agent-to-agent calls are not an ungoverned side channel.

steps.title: Per-user credential injection
steps.what: The caller's gateway key is never forwarded to the agent; only the credential the Auth Mode supplies reaches it.
steps.why: Agents that call other agents need the same sign-in, policy and logging as tool traffic, so agent-to-agent calls are not an ungoverned side channel.
